Give me five minutes — AI automation, explained completely Here's the secret the whole thing stands on: every serious app you use can send and receive messages — to EACH OTHER, no human in between. Something happens in one app, it announces it with the details attached, and any app you choose can be listening. Watch it once: someone fills your form → the form app announces "new entry" with the answers inside → your spreadsheet catches it and writes the row → that new row is itself an announcement → your email app catches it and sends the welcome, personalized by name. Three apps had a conversation. From the click on, no human touched anything. That's an automation: WHEN this happens, DO that. And how you build one surprises everyone: you DRAW it. A canvas. Apps are blocks, messages are lines. The code already exists — the app makers wrote it and left the doors open. If you can sketch your process on a whiteboard, you have the whole skill. Plain automations hit a wall: rails only handle same-every-time. The moment a step needs reading and judging — is this email angry or urgent? — you drop a BRAIN into the flow. The message pauses, the AI reads it, decides, and routes: complaint → priority plus a drafted apology; invoice question → the accounting sheet; kind words → a warm reply waiting for your okay. One flow, three outcomes, decided fresh every time. Rails for the movement, judgment at the junctions. Chain enough of these and whole jobs run themselves. Businesses pay real money every month for exactly this — and the skill takes weeks, because the hard part was never code. It's the thinking: map the flow, pick the rules, place the brain. You never write the code. You draw the conversation. #aiautomation #professorglitch #aiagent
